sections.overview: The European Golden Plover is a migratory shorebird of northern Eurasia.
sections.identification: Its upperparts are golden-spangled; in breeding plumage the face and underparts become largely black, while the underwing and axillaries are white. Compared with the Pacific Golden Plover (P. fulva), the white axillaries are a useful flight character. The Grey Plover (P. squatarola) has black axillaries instead.
sections.habitat: It breeds on moors, peatlands and tundra, then winters mainly on open grassland and farmland, with some use of coasts and wetlands.
sections.diet: It takes ground-dwelling invertebrates such as insects, earthworms and snails, and may also eat berries, seeds and grass.
sections.behavior: Most populations migrate toward western and southern Europe in winter; cold weather can trigger movements farther south.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground in a shallow scrape in open, short vegetation.
sections.ecology: Its migration is generally shorter and more focused on Europe than that of its close relative, the Pacific Golden Plover (Pluvialis fulva), which breeds in Siberia and Alaska and winters widely around the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
sections.conservation: In the United Kingdom, the species is on the RSPB’s Green List; that national rating does not replace a global assessment.
